name: Rupert Lowe
role: UK MP for Great Yarmouth (since 2024); leader of Restore Britain (founded 2025); former Brexit Party MEP and Southampton FC chairman
summary: Lowe is a businessman-turned-politician who sits on the nationalist right. He campaigns for mass deportation and net-negative immigration, repeal of the Human Rights Act and withdrawal from the ECHR, cutting the state, tax and welfare, ending Net Zero, defunding the BBC and restoring free speech, with a socially conservative, Christian-heritage cultural agenda. He frames himself as an individualist opposed to statism and globalism, and rejects the 'ethno-nationalist' label while arguing for the demographic continuity of Britain's historic peoples.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Restore Britain's economic paper says healthcare stays free at the point of use for citizens as a non-negotiable principle; non-citizens would pay market rates.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The economic paper he introduced lists minimum wages among the regulations that fetter private business; no support for raising it appears.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Argues the state has crowded out the private sector as the engine of wealth creation and that state micromanagement distorts organic price mechanisms.

public-ownership.rationale: Energy paper says Restore is 'not dogmatic' between privatisation and nationalisation ('what works is best'); economic paper cites state firms like Equinor as able to succeed, but wants a smaller state overall.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Platform abolishes inheritance tax and stamp duty, cuts corporation and income tax; he says top earners ('rain-makers') are being driven out by tax rises.

unions-good.rationale: Criticism of particular militant unions is nearby; no stated general position on unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Platform names private property rights a cornerstone and says inheritance tax and wealth taxes conflict with private property principles.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Told Parliament 'you do not regulate for growth, you deregulate' and called for disbanding the FCA and PRA; platform proposes repealing a quarter-century of regulation by default.

cut-welfare.rationale: Platform freezes working-age benefits, aims to save £70-80bn a year and says the welfare system rewards indolence more than work.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Platform would repeal hate speech and incitement to hatred laws and restore free speech traditions on a statutory footing.

state-harmful.rationale: Says 'I hate the state and I love the individual' and that the state has become the enemy of the British people, but also says a state is needed for defence and the law and wants a 'small, judicious' one.

limit-guns.rationale: Opposed merging firearms licences in a Commons debate, said responsible owners are not the problem, and criticised the 1990s handgun ban; is himself a shotgun and firearms holder.

empower-police-military.rationale: Platform calls for widespread stop and search and to rebuild and rearm Britain and the army (voted for a Conservative defence readiness motion), though his policing paper says police problems are structural, not funding.

traditional-family.rationale: Platform says strong families underpin a thriving society and puts pro-family policy at its heart; speaks of marriage and Christian upbringing as the aim.

more-religion-public.rationale: Platform calls Britain an historically Christian country guided by Christian morality, to strengthen teaching of Christian heritage and protect churches, framed as historical literacy rather than instruction.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Platform abolishes 'every trace of DEI', opposes decolonisation teaching and racial preferences; says racism is racism even when white people are on the receiving end.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Platform says biological sex is not a social construct and rejects 'gender ideology'; does not separately discuss gender as distinct from sex.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Core platform theme: protect British culture, reverse cultural change from mass immigration, teach pride in British history and culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Says he does not believe in conserving or reforming the status quo and wants a 'democratic revolution', while also appealing to the 1689 Bill of Rights and constitutional tradition.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Platform: reverse mass immigration, net negative migration, end low-skilled and third-world immigration, deport illegal migrants.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Platform condemns 'globalist' approach, would leave the ECHR, remove the Refugee Convention from domestic law and end foreign aid.

free-trade.rationale: Describes the British as 'libertarian free traders' and criticises the EU as a protectionist bloc; the platform also uses remittance taxes and visa/trade measures against countries refusing returns.

nation-first.rationale: Platform: 'Put British Interests First', ending the globalist approach and cutting aid that does not serve national interest.

open-borders.rationale: Platform wants mass deportations and an end to the asylum system; says borders matter and rejects the idea of no borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Platform wants cheap, abundant energy and rapid growth and repeal of Net Zero; tax cuts targeted at growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Platform would repeal the Climate Change Act and Net Zero; says climate change cannot be proved and calls 'luxury beliefs' around Net Zero harmful (energy paper concedes some greenhouse effect).

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy paper proposes a nationwide small modular reactor programme and accelerated nuclear expansion; he backs nuclear.

experts-over-public.rationale: Repeatedly attacks unelected quangos and experts (SAGE, MHRA) and wants power returned to elected representatives and the public, including binding referendums.

central-planning.rationale: Calls the British economy a 'corporatist command economy' akin to the USSR and says central planners always get it wrong.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Platform abolishes inheritance tax, calling it an envy-based death tax; opposed the farm inheritance tax change.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Opposes 'state-led micromanagement' of the economy, though the platform treats energy as strategic infrastructure and offers incentives for domestic manufacturing.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Attacks central banks and QE, but his paper keeps the Bank of England with tight control of money supply and only considers a gold standard as a long-term option.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Says the King is constitutionally very important as titular head and Defender of the Faith, while criticising the King's conduct on faiths and multiculturalism.

direct-votes.rationale: Platform proposes a binding referendum on restoring the death penalty and he questioned changes (jury trials) without an electoral mandate.

separate-church-state.rationale: Wants Christian morality to guide governance, special protection for churches and the King as Defender of the (Anglican) faith.

military-superiority.rationale: Calls to rearm are nearby; no stated position on superiority over rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Belonging paper wants the White British historic majority to remain predominant ('demographic security') but rejects ethnic purity and the ethno-nationalist label; mixed.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Platform says the economy should reward grafters, calls inheritance tax envy-driven and says the state rewards indolence; criticises schools where winning is seen as bad.

restore-past-order.rationale: Platform and name ('Restore Britain'; says Britain worked far better a generation ago) point one way, but the belonging paper says 'we cannot simply turn the clock back'.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Platform says 'objective truth, not ideology, must guide governance'; says he is founded on common sense.

media-academia-power.rationale: Says universities originated destructive ideas that dominate political life and calls the BBC 'poison'; argues quangos and the civil service, not only media, hold power.

total-state.rationale: Platform wants a light-touch state and calls the existing state an overreaching 'command economy'; opposes digital ID and state intrusion.

national-rebirth.rationale: Says Britons are 'a shell of our former selves' and calls for a 'democratic revolution' rather than reform.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Platform aims to balance the budget and cut debt, and he proposed banning quantitative easing; says nations cannot tax themselves to prosperity.

economic-freedom.rationale: Quotes Hayek on planning and links sound money, private property and a light-touch state to a free society.

national-self-determination.rationale: Says he likes 'competing nation states with an accountable parliament' and wants sovereignty over borders, fishing and law.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Platform restricts all working-age benefits to British citizens, ends benefits for ILR holders and foreign nationals.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Platform would deny benefits to able-bodied claimants who refuse work such as litter picking.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Platform creates a fund to preserve historic churches and Christian heritage.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Platform and energy paper lift the North Sea ban, expand oil, gas and shale.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Platform would deport those who fail to integrate or reject British culture; says immigrants must accept the country's culture and laws.

elite-replacement.rationale: Calls mass immigration a long deceitful plan by elites, Labour put power ahead of principle, and says 'replaced' is the correct word; also rejects ethnic purity.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Told Rogan women now hold an 'omnipotent position' in British society.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Describes the political class, civil service and quangos as corrupt and out of touch.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Says he wants a minimal state and an Austrian-school approach, but the platform keeps a free NHS, state schools and pensions.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Belonging paper says citizens are equal before the law and 'men and women are morally equal', but not identical treatment as policy.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Opposes Sharia courts and says everyone must live under one law.

population-transfer.rationale: Platform pressures legally resident foreign nationals who don't integrate or commit crime to leave via a hostile environment, remittance tax and deportation; applied to non-citizens.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Said Europe's progress came from dynamic tension between nation states and war, and praises competition and 'a degree of Darwinism'.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Platform says mass immigration has made Britain less culturally and socially cohesive; cites Lebanon.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Economic paper blames price controls as fetters on business and says state micromanagement distorts prices.

party-controls-media.rationale: Platform: no state censorship of lawful speech, repeal the Online Safety Act.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Platform and belonging paper say citizenship thresholds are far too low and citizenship would be granted only in tiny numbers.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Says leaving the EU was about sovereignty and the pound; the EU is an unaccountable superstate.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Platform places free expression on a statutory footing and bars state censorship of lawful content.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Calling degrees bogus is nearby; no stated position on graduates being out of touch.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Describes clannish South Asian cultures as incompatible with a high-trust Christian society; avoids calling cultures higher or lower.

death-penalty.rationale: Platform calls for a binding referendum on restoring the death penalty and says it is just to execute the guilty of the most heinous crimes; he asked the Prime Minister to hold one.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Wants a ban on halal and kosher slaughter: 'no religious exemptions, one rule for all'.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Platform ends foreign aid that does not serve British interests.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Economic paper criticises Bank of England independence since 1997 and would require Chancellor authorisation for monetary expansion.

common-currency.rationale: Campaigned in 1997 to save the pound; says losing your currency means losing sovereignty.

no-bailouts.rationale: Ten Minute Rule Bill speech criticises the 2008 bailouts of financial institutions and QE as shielding firms from capitalism's discipline.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Great Clarification Act would let Parliament overturn court rulings obstructing the democratic will on immigration, though he also invokes Bill of Rights protections.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Platform abolishes DEI in government and says football and organisations should rest on merit alone.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Platform wants school and university teaching centred on British history and Christian heritage.

patriotic-education.rationale: Platform: 'a pro-British education system' proud of history, culture and people.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Platform abolishes DEI and calls racially exclusive job adverts racism; called for removing Fulham's ad excluding white men.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Told Commons that clubs advertising coaching roles that exclude white men were racist and should be withdrawn.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Says Parliament should be omnipotent under the 1689 Bill of Rights; Great Clarification Act asserts parliamentary sovereignty over courts.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Argued in Commons that non-stun slaughter inflicts agony and animals feel everything; wants it banned.

animal-use-humane.rationale: A farmer who says livestock should have swift, painless deaths; objects to non-stun slaughter, not to farming.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Says he would be 'doing less than my duty' not to fight politically despite being rich enough to retire.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Energy paper: 'no foreign power should own any component of our energy infrastructure'.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Platform says it will use state power to help families have more children, e.g. through childcare, rather than immigration.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Requesting and promising to publish data is nearby; no stated position on a legal right of access.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Platform would leave the ECHR, repeal the Human Rights Act and remove the Refugee Convention from domestic law.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Economic paper makes private health costs tax deductible and gives schools independence funded per pupil.

suppress-opposition.rationale: General defence of free speech is a principle, not a stated position on suppressing opposition.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Platform repeals the Gender Recognition Act and bars legal sex change; opposes men in women-only spaces.

assisted-dying.rationale: Voted against the Terminally Ill Adults Bill at third reading and platform would repeal it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Told Bret Weinstein he does not consider himself left or right but 'founded on common sense'.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Platform says it will reverse the 'Islamisation of Britain' and he calls Islamic cultural codes on women incompatible with British society, while accepting integrated Muslims.

social-market-economy.rationale: Combines market reform with a 'robust social safety net' for the vulnerable and free NHS for citizens.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Platform: rebuild and rearm Britain's armed forces.

racial-franchise.rationale: States that citizens of all ethnic backgrounds are British and equal before the law.

open-government-data.rationale: Promises to publish internal Home Office and Treasury data and SAGE modelling.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Platform promotes Christian heritage and church preservation.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Platform expands policing, stop and search, detention and imprisonment, and would restore the death penalty.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Platform bans all foreign nationals, including Commonwealth citizens, from voting at any level.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Platform restores a right to use lethal force to defend home and family.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Belonging paper stresses 'continuity between past, present and future' of the historic peoples of Britain, while noting the population was never homogeneous.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Platform: 'Biological sex is not a social construct. It is a fixed trait.'

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Platform and Commons statement: biological sex is immutable and men may not access women-only spaces.

person-over-state.rationale: Told Commons that government should serve the people, not the other way round, and opposes digital ID as treating citizens as suspects.

racial-pride.rationale: Belonging paper says nothing is shameful in acknowledging English, Welsh, Scottish ethnic identities and concern for the White British population is not inherently racist.

communal-electorates.rationale: Platform would end 'ethnoreligious bloc voting' and abolish mass postal voting.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Economic paper abolishes the Emissions Trading Scheme and Climate Change Levy; platform ends Carbon Price Support.

arms-reduction.rationale: Platform wants to rebuild and rearm Britain.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Policy paper abolishes interest on all student loans held by British nationals, including accrued interest.

public-service-media.rationale: Platform would defund the BBC and make it a subscription service.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Platform repeals Net Zero and treats it as an attack on freedom.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Calls for strict sentences are nearby; no stated position on sentences fixed by law.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Platform deports legally resident foreigners who cannot speak English and requires English for spousal visas.

national-church-status.rationale: Says the monarch's constitutional role as Defender of the Faith means the Church of England and that the King should uphold it.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Economic paper cuts VAT to 18%, raises the threshold, and abolishes insurance premium tax and air passenger duty.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Platform aims to end 'political Islam and other forms of ethnoreligious bloc voting'.

national-resource-control.rationale: Platform: no foreign ownership of energy infrastructure and 'take back our seas'; Commons speech seeks full British control of the EEZ.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Says Britain is a very tolerant country and he does not believe white Britons to be racist.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Platform rewards 'grafters' and puts British workers first.

notes: Left Reform UK in 2025 (whip suspended March 2025) and now leads Restore Britain, registered as a party in March 2026. Party documents are published under his leadership and often with his foreword, so they are treated as his positions. Answers use his most recent positions (2025-2026). Positions before 2024 (Referendum Party 1997, Brexit Party MEP 2019-20) were not separately documented from primary text and are not used. Foreign policy (Ukraine, Israel), abortion, same-sex marriage and drug policy were searched and left null for lack of his own statements.
